bio: Arif Hayat Nairang is a sociocultural anthropologist interested in virtual cultures, studies of play and humor, anthropology of emotions, and environmental anthropology.

His book manuscript, Surplus Life: Play and Laughter in Rural Kashmir examines how people indulge in playful thinking in everyday life not only to bring relief but also as a way to perceive, imagine, and craft possible worlds.

His future research projects include a cross-cultural ethnography of online gaming and a study of the fraught emotional ties between humans and birds in Gharana, a small wetland located along the international border in Jammu.
As an educator, Arif embraces a play-based, embodied, and experiential pedagogy that has been recognized by students and institutions alike.
